author: David Reed
summary: Wires and governs the case_precedents institutional-memory RAG collection. chg-14: deterministic precedent id + upsert (the B6 unstable-key anti-pattern). chg-15: the scope guard governs the two REAL collections (nccn_guidelines, case_precedents) instead of a phantom 'clinical_guidelines' never queried. chg-16: the /feedback write gets an IntentRecord, a scope-guarded write, and audit-before-write. Loop proven end-to-end: a precedent flipped a case IN_REVIEW -> AUTO_APPROVED.

changes.description: add_precedent uses a deterministic sha256 content id (_precedent_id) and upsert instead of f"prec_{abs(hash(case_summary))}" + add. The same override is now idempotent and a corrected override overwrites in place.
changes.failure_pattern: The same Medical Director override produced a different precedent id on every server restart (silent duplicate precedents accumulating), and a same-process repeat collided on ChromaDB .add() and raised.
changes.root_cause: The id was f"prec_{abs(hash(case_summary))}". Python's hash(str) is per-process randomized (PYTHONHASHSEED), so it is unstable across processes; and .add() rejects a duplicate id rather than updating. Same class as the B6 decision_id bug: a derived/unstable value used as a storage key.

evidence.note: Returned 5179595735129669111 then 5777744012722371097 for the identical string, demonstrating the per-process instability.

Pre-fix, re-adding the same scenario keeps the stale document (add ignores duplicate ids); the id-determinism test would fail on hash(). Post-fix: idempotent, deterministic content id, update-in-place; 5 tests pass.

predicted_fixes: The same override upserts to one stable id across restarts (no duplicate accumulation).
A corrected override overwrites the prior document in place.
The id is deterministic and content-keyed.
risk_cases: Existing precedents written under the old hash-based ids remain in the store with their old ids; they are retrieved by similarity regardless of id, so no data loss. New writes use the stable id.
A precedent whose scenario text changes gets a new id (a new precedent); intended.
changes.why_this_component: The bug is in how the precedent is stored (id + write mode), a property of the retriever's tool implementation, not the agent's reasoning.
changes.rollback_plan: git revert the chg-14 commit. Restores add() + hash id. No migration; the store's existing entries are unaffected.

changes.description: The scope guard's collection model now names the two real ChromaDB collections (nccn_guidelines, case_precedents) via SSOT constants; IntentRecord.allowed_collections lists them; the submit route guards the RAG query against each real collection. Replaces a phantom 'clinical_guidelines' that was never queried.
changes.failure_pattern: The P-4 minimum-necessary guard governed a fiction: IntentRecord declared allowed_collections=['clinical_guidelines'], the submit route's rag.query scope check named 'clinical_guidelines', but the live retriever reads nccn_guidelines and case_precedents. The two real collections — including institutional-memory precedents — were entirely ungoverned.
changes.root_cause: The intent constant and the route both used a name that no longer matched the retriever's collections after the dual-collection store landed; the guard's collection check was therefore always a no-op.

evidence.note: Pre-fix: PRIOR_AUTH_ALLOWED_COLLECTIONS=['clinical_guidelines']; retriever __init__ creates nccn_guidelines and case_precedents. The route's enforce_scope named clinical_guidelines with a comment admitting its enforcement value was nil.
New drift test asserts intent.allowed_collections == vector_store.RAG_COLLECTIONS, and that the guard denies an unlisted collection while allowing the two real ones.

predicted_fixes: IntentRecord for prior-auth allows exactly the two real collections; the phantom is gone.
A submit RAG query to any collection outside the declared scope fail-closes.
case_precedents is now within the governed minimum-necessary scope.
risk_cases: The submit route now issues two rag.query scope checks (one per collection); audit-trail wiring tests updated to the new order.
Any external reference to the 'clinical_guidelines' collection name (dead rag/pipeline.py still uses it internally, but that path never runs).
changes.why_this_component: The scope guard is the P-4 minimum-necessary middleware; the defect and fix live in the collection model it enforces against.
changes.rollback_plan: git revert chg-15. Restores the phantom collection name; the guard reverts to a no-op collection check. No migration.

changes.description: The /feedback precedent write is governed like the submit path: a narrow institutional_learning IntentRecord (case_precedents + rag.write_precedent/audit.append only) declared as the first audit event, a scope-guarded write (fail-closed 403), and the learning event audited before the ChromaDB write. Rule 3 of the scope guard now covers any rag.* action.
changes.failure_pattern: learn_from_feedback wrote a precedent to the case_precedents RAG collection with no IntentRecord, no scope guard, and add_precedent running BEFORE the audit — the only RAG mutation outside the P-3/P-4/P-5 governance the submit route enforces.
changes.root_cause: The endpoint predated the governance rollout and was never brought under it; the scope guard's collection check also only applied to rag.query, not writes.

evidence.note: add_precedent at line 356 ran before the sole audit.log at line 368; no IntentRecord, no enforce_scope.

Asserts intent.declared is the first event, a scope.allow is recorded for the precedent write, the learning event is audited before add_precedent, and the feedback intent is scoped to case_precedents only (no guideline read, no DB writes).

predicted_fixes: A /feedback call emits intent.declared first, scope-guards the write to case_precedents, and audits the learning event before the write.
A precedent write to any other collection fail-closes to 403.
The feedback intent cannot read guidelines or write DB business rows.
risk_cases: Rule 3 now applies to all rag.* actions; a future rag.* action without a collection_name would be denied (collection_missing) — intended fail-closed behavior.
In enforce mode a genuine scope violation now 403s instead of silently writing; never fires in correct operation.
changes.why_this_component: Bringing an ungoverned state-changing endpoint under the P-4 scope guard and the pre-write-audit invariant is a middleware-tier change.
changes.rollback_plan: git revert chg-16. Restores the ungoverned write-then-audit endpoint and the rag.query-only Rule 3. No migration.

verified_fixes: 5 precedent tests pass: idempotent same-scenario write, distinct scenarios kept, update-in-place, deterministic content id, write->retrieve round-trip.
End-to-end this session: /feedback -> embed -> retrieve -> decision flipped a case IN_REVIEW -> AUTO_APPROVED with the rationale attributing it to the precedent.
Drift test asserts intent.allowed_collections == RAG_COLLECTIONS; guard denies an unlisted collection and allows the two real ones.
Submit route guards the RAG query against each real collection; audit-trail tests updated to the two-collection order.
verified_risks: The two-rag.query-guard change was reflected in test_run_sites_are_scope_guarded without weakening it.

verified_fixes: test_feedback_governed: intent.declared first, scope.allow recorded for the write, learning event audited before add_precedent, feedback intent scoped to case_precedents only.
Scope-guard Rule 3 now covers rag.* actions without regressing the existing scope-guard probes.
verdicts.notes: Full unit suite 681 passed; ruff + PHI-guard clean.
